name: Prime Minister's Office (former PM Secretariat), public exterior only
assumptions: Height is not published: every height is fitted from one head-on street photo with a reconstructed camera, so expect 1 to 2 m error; the top of the main dome is about 34.6 m and the flag pole 37 m.
Seven storeys comes from a 2016 government press release (pid.gov.pk); the storey split on each wing is read from the photos.
Plan is made symmetric about the entrance axis on the dossier wing axis; turret centres from satellite imagery are sheared by several degrees, so positions can be off by up to about 6 m.
Rear wing elevations were not photographed: built with the same storey bands as the front.
Rear inner turrets (u about 10 and 30 at the back) heights are guesses.
Central core rear half and the spine blocks are from the roof plan only; their heights are guesses.
The courtyard second dome is placed from the plan view; the base block under it is a guess.
Courtyards are left open at ground level; dark glazed roof strips seen from the air are not modelled.
Forecourt pavilion is sized from the head-on photo; its side faces are guesses and its garden is not modelled.
Entrance ramp seen in a close photo is simplified to a flight of steps; entrance details omitted.
Long pale strips on the SW are omitted because their nature (water or paving) is unconfirmed.
Wall, tower and glazing colours are estimates from photos in varied light; dome and terracotta hexes are dossier values from satellite imagery; night glow is estimated.
Arcade and window counts are bay rhythm estimates, not counted exactly.
